subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody drug conjugates

steps.tx: Monoclonal antibodies are **immunoglobulins** made from a single B cell clone, so every molecule binds one epitope. In practice, IgG is the class used almost exclusively for therapeutic monoclonal antibodies. The Fab arms carry the **complementarity-determining regions (CDRs)** that set specificity and affinity, while the Fc region recruits immune effectors and drives antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and complement activation.
steps.say: Monoclonal antibodies are immunoglobulins produced from one B cell clone, so each molecule recognises a single epitope. In practice, IgG is almost always the class chosen for therapy. The Fab arms hold the complementarity-determining regions, which determine specificity and affinity. The Fc region recruits immune effectors, driving antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and complement activation.

steps.tx: Antibody names carry a **nomenclature stem** that signals their origin. **Chimeric** antibodies keep murine variable regions fused to human constant regions, as with cetuximab. **Humanised** antibodies, such as trastuzumab and bevacizumab, retain only the mouse complementarity-determining regions grafted onto a human framework. Because greater murine content drives **anti-drug antibody** formation, a more human sequence is generally less immunogenic.

steps.tx: Oncology monoclonal antibodies work through two broad routes. Some **block signalling** by binding a receptor on the tumour cell surface, which stops ligands from activating it or stops receptor pairs from forming, so growth messages are lost. Others rely on the **Fc region** to recruit immune effector mechanisms, namely **antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity** and **complement-dependent cytotoxicity**. Some antibodies also trap soluble growth factors before they reach their receptors.
steps.say: Oncology monoclonal antibodies work in two broad ways. Some block signalling, binding a receptor on the tumour cell so that its growth messages cannot be received. Others use their Fc region to recruit immune killing, through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and complement-dependent cytotoxicity. Some also trap a soluble growth factor so it cannot reach its receptor.

left.title: Signalling blockade
points: Binds a receptor on the tumour cell
Stops ligand activation or receptor pairing

steps.tx: Key toxicities are **infusion reactions**, **cardiotoxicity** and **neutropenia**. Trastuzumab causes LVEF decline, and anthracycline co-therapy raises severe cardiotoxicity risk about three to four times. Sacituzumab causes neutropenia and diarrhoea; UGT1A1 variants raise toxicity, so dose reduction is preemptive. Febrile neutropenia calls for holding the dose, reducing it and giving growth-factor support. Cetuximab requires KRAS wild-type status, as codon 12 mutations predict non-response.
